THE MONTGOMERY REVOCABLE LIVING TRUST 
AGREEMENT
A Joint Revocable Inter Vivos Trust for Multi-State Probate Avoidance & Blended Family 
Protection
THIS REVOCABLE LIVING TRUST AGREEMENT (the "Trust Agreement") is made and 
entered into this 12th day of November, 2026, by and between RICHARD STERLING 
MONTGOMERY and ELEANOR VANCE MONTGOMERY, spouses residing in Houston, Harris 
County, State of Texas (hereinafter collectively referred to as the "Grantors" and individually as 
a "Grantor"), and RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY and ELEANOR VANCE 
MONTGOMERY as Initial Co-Trustees (hereinafter collectively referred to with any successor 
trustee(s) as the "Trustee").
Article I: TRUST NAME, FAMILY DECLARATIONS, AND TRUST FUNDING
Section 1.01 Name of Trust. This trust shall be known as "THE MONTGOMERY REVOCABLE 
LIVING TRUST, dated November 12, 2026" and may be referred to as such in all deeds, 
financial account titles, beneficiary designations, and legal instruments.
Section 1.02 Blended Family & Children Declarations. Grantors are lawfully married. Grantor 
1 (Richard Sterling Montgomery) has 1 child from a prior marriage, namely: Harrison 
Montgomery (DOB: 06/14/2005). Grantor 2 (Eleanor Vance Montgomery) has 1 child from a 
prior marriage, namely: Beatrice Vance (DOB: 09/22/2008). Together, Grantors have 1 joint 
child of this marriage, namely: Ethan Montgomery (DOB: 11/05/2015), who is a beneficiary with 
special needs.
Section 1.03 Initial Funding & Multi-State Real Property. Grantors hereby assign, convey, 
transfer, and deliver to the Trustee all property listed on Schedule A (Joint/Community 
Property), Schedule B (Separate Property of Grantor 1), and Schedule C (Separate Property of 
Grantor 2) attached hereto, including the primary residence located in Texas and the vacation 
real property located in New Mexico, to be held, administered, and distributed in accordance 
with the terms of this Agreement so as to avoid both domiciliary and ancillary probate.
Article II: ADMINISTRATION DURING JOINT LIFETIMES & RESERVATION 
OF RIGHTS
Section 2.01 Distributions During Joint Lifetimes. During the joint lifetimes of the Grantors, 
the Trustee shall distribute to or for the benefit of the Grantors so much of the net income and 
principal of the community/joint trust estate as either Grantor may direct, or as the Trustee 
deems necessary for the Grantors' health, education, maintenance, and support ("HEMS") in 
their accustomed standard of living.
Section 2.02 Right to Amend or Revoke. While both Grantors are living and have legal 
capacity, this Trust may be amended, modified, or restated only by a signed written instrument 
executed by both Grantors and delivered to the Trustee. Either Grantor may unilaterally revoke

this Trust as to their respective community/joint one-half share or separate property upon written 
notice to the other Grantor and the Trustee.
Section 2.03 Incapacity of a Grantor. A Grantor shall be deemed incapacitated upon (a) 
written certification by two licensed physicians (one of whom is the Grantor's attending 
physician) that the Grantor is unable to effectively manage their financial affairs, or (b) a court 
determination of incapacity. During any period of incapacity of one Grantor, the other Grantor 
shall serve as sole Trustee.
Article III: DIVISION INTO SUB-TRUSTS UPON DEATH OF FIRST GRANTOR 
(A-B-C / QTIP STRUCTURE)
Section 3.01 Mandatory Division at First Death. Upon the death of the first Grantor to die (the 
"Deceased Grantor"), the surviving Grantor (the "Surviving Grantor") shall have NO power to 
amend, revoke, or alter the disposition of the Deceased Grantor's share of the Trust Estate. The 
Trustee shall divide the Trust Estate (including any assets received via the Deceased Grantor's 
Pour-Over Will or beneficiary designations) into three separate trusts:
Section 3.02 The Survivor's Trust (Trust A - Revocable). The Survivor's Trust shall consist of 
the Surviving Grantor's one-half (1/2) interest in the joint/community estate and all of the 
Surviving Grantor's separate property (Schedule B or C). The Survivor's Trust shall remain 
revocable and amendable by the Surviving Grantor during their lifetime.
Section 3.03 The Credit Shelter / Family Bypass Trust (Trust B - Irrevocable). If applicable 
for estate tax or blended family protection, the Bypass Trust shall hold an amount of the 
Deceased Grantor's share designated in the Sub-Trust Addendum. Trust B is irrevocable upon 
the first death.
Section 3.04 The Marital QTIP Trust (Trust C - Irrevocable Blended Family Lock). The 
balance of the Deceased Grantor's share shall be allocated to the Qualified Terminable Interest 
Property ("QTIP") Marital Trust under IRC § 2056(b)(7), administered under the QTIP 
Addendum. The Surviving Grantor shall receive all net income at least annually for life, but shall 
have NO power to divert principal to a new spouse or disinherit the Deceased Grantor's 
biological children.
Article IV: DISTRIBUTION UPON DEATH OF SURVIVING GRANTOR
Section 4.01 Allocation Among Descendants & Special Needs Sub-Trust. Upon the death 
of the Surviving Grantor, the remaining balance of the Marital QTIP Trust (and Bypass Trust) 
shall pass strictly as directed by the Deceased Grantor's schedule of remainder beneficiaries, 
and the Survivor's Trust shall pass as directed by the Surviving Grantor:
(a) 60% to the Staggered Distribution Children's Sub-Trusts (administered with HEMS guardrails 
and age 25/30/35 principal releases);
(b) 40% to the Third-Party Supplemental / Special Needs Trust for the benefit of Ethan 
Montgomery, so as not to disqualify said beneficiary from Medicaid or SSI.

Article V: TRUSTEE SUCCESSION, POWERS, AND SPENDTHRIFT 
PROTECTION
Section 5.01 Nomination of Successor Trustees. Upon the death, resignation, or incapacity 
of both Initial Co-Trustees, the following shall serve as Successor Trustee in the order named:
1. First Successor Trustee: Julian M. Montgomery, Austin, TX
2. Second Successor Trustee: Clara Vance, Houston, TX
3. Corporate / Independent Fiduciary Backup: Texas Capital Trust Company
Section 5.02 Spendthrift Clause. No interest of any beneficiary in the income or principal of 
any trust created hereunder shall be subject to anticipation, assignment, pledge, sale, or 
transfer in any manner, nor shall any beneficiary's interest be liable for or subject to the debts, 
contracts, liabilities, engagements, torts, lawsuits, bankruptcy, or marital dissolution/alimony 
claims of any beneficiary or their spouse.
Section 5.03 Governing Law. The validity, construction, and administration of this Trust shall 
be governed by the laws of the State of Texas.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Grantors and Initial Co-Trustees have executed this Revocable 
Living Trust Agreement as of the day and year first written above.

RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY, Grantor & Co-Trustee

LAST WILL AND TESTAMENT (POUR-OVER WILL)
of RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY — With Minor Child Guardianship 
Nominations
I, RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY, residing in Houston, Harris County, State of Texas, 
being of sound mind and disposing memory, do hereby make, publish, and declare this 
instrument to be my Last Will and Testament (specifically structured as a "Pour-Over Will" to 
operate in conjunction with my Revocable Living Trust), hereby revoking all prior wills and 
codicils heretofore made by me.
Article I: FAMILY IDENTIFICATION & BLENDED FAMILY DECLARATIONS
Section 1.01 Spouse and Children. I am married to Eleanor Vance Montgomery. My child 
from a prior relationship is Harrison Montgomery (DOB: 06/14/2005), and my joint child born of 
my current marriage is Ethan Montgomery (DOB: 11/05/2015).
Article II: DISPOSITION OF TANGIBLE PERSONAL PROPERTY
Section 2.01 Personal Effects. I give and bequeath all of my clothing, jewelry, household 
furniture, automobiles, and other tangible personal property not already titled in my Revocable 
Living Trust (and not disposed of by a signed Personal Property Memorandum) to my spouse, 
Eleanor Vance Montgomery, if she survives me by thirty (30) days; and if not, to the Trustee of 
the Trust identified in Article III below.
Article III: POUR-OVER OF RESIDUARY ESTATE TO REVOCABLE LIVING 
TRUST
Section 3.01 Pour-Over Devise to Living Trust. I give, devise, and bequeath all the rest, 
residue, and remainder of my probate estate, of every kind and character and wheresoever 
situated, which I may own or have any interest in at the time of my death and which was 
inadvertently omitted from or not titled in my Trust prior to my death, to the then-acting Trustee 
of "THE MONTGOMERY REVOCABLE LIVING TRUST, dated November 12, 2026" executed 
prior to (or concurrently with) the execution of this Will, to be added to the principal of said Trust 
and held, administered, subdivided into the Marital QTIP, Children's Staggered, and Special 
Needs Sub-Trusts, and distributed in accordance with the terms of said Trust Agreement.
Section 3.02 Savings Incorporation by Reference. If for any reason the aforesaid Revocable 
Living Trust is not in existence at the time of my death, or if the devise under Section 3.01 is 
held invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, I hereby incorporate by reference the terms and 
provisions of said Trust Agreement as it existed on the date of execution of this Will, and direct 
that my Residuary Estate be held and administered by my Executor as Trustee of a 
testamentary trust on those identical terms.

Article IV: NOMINATION OF GUARDIAN FOR MINOR OR INCAPACITATED 
CHILDREN
Section 4.01 Guardian of the Person. If my spouse does not survive me, or is adjudicated 
incapacitated, and at my death any child of mine is a minor (under eighteen (18) years of age) 
or requires adult guardianship due to special needs, I nominate and appoint Julian M. 
Montgomery, residing at 1040 West Peachtree St, Austin, TX 78701, Relationship: Brother, to 
serve as Guardian of the Person of my minor or incapacitated child(ren).
Section 4.02 Alternate Guardian of the Person. If Julian M. Montgomery is unable or 
unwilling to serve, I nominate and appoint Clara Vance, residing at 1802 South Congress Ave, 
Houston, TX 77019, Relationship: Sister-in-Law, as Alternate Guardian of the Person.
Section 4.03 Waiver of Bond for Guardian. I direct that no Guardian nominated herein shall 
be required to post any bond or security in any jurisdiction.
Article V: APPOINTMENT OF INDEPENDENT EXECUTOR
Section 5.01 Executor Designation. I nominate and appoint Eleanor Vance Montgomery as 
Independent Executor of this Pour-Over Will, and Julian M. Montgomery as Successor 
Independent Executor, to serve without bond and free of court supervision to the maximum 
extent permitted by state law.
Section 5.02 Tax Elections & DSUE Portability. My Executor is expressly authorized to 
coordinate with the Trustee of my Revocable Living Trust regarding the filing of federal and 
state estate tax returns (Form 706), the Qualified Terminable Interest Property (QTIP) election 
under IRC § 2056(b)(7), and the Deceased Spousal Unused Exclusion ("DSUE") portability 
election.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I, RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY, have signed this Pour-
Over Will on this 12th day of November, 2026.

MARITAL QTIP TRUST & STAGGERED CHILDREN'S SUB-
TRUSTS
Irrevocable Blended Family Sub-Trust & Age-Staggered HEMS Distribution Instrument
THIS SUB-TRUST ADMINISTRATION INSTRUMENT governs the administration of (1) The 
Marital QTIP Trust for the Blended Family, and (2) The Separate Staggered-Distribution Sub-
Trusts for the Grantors' Children under The Montgomery Revocable Living Trust.
Part I: THE MARITAL QTIP SUB-TRUST (BLENDED FAMILY PROTECTION)
Section 1.01 Purpose & Irrevocability. Upon the death of the Deceased Grantor (Richard 
Sterling Montgomery), the Marital QTIP Sub-Trust is strictly IRREVOCABLE. Its dual purpose is 
to provide financial security for the Surviving Spouse (Eleanor Vance Montgomery) during her 
remaining lifetime while legally guaranteeing that the remaining principal passes upon the 
Surviving Spouse's death to the Deceased Grantor's designated biological/adopted children 
(Harrison Montgomery and Ethan Montgomery).
Section 1.02 Mandatory Income to Surviving Spouse (IRC § 2056(b)(7)). The Trustee shall 
pay to or apply for the benefit of the Surviving Spouse all of the net income of the Marital QTIP 
Trust in quarterly or more frequent installments during the Surviving Spouse's lifetime. The 
Surviving Spouse shall have the right to require the Trustee to make any unproductive property 
in the Marital QTIP Trust productive or to convert it into income-producing property within a 
reasonable time.
Section 1.03 Ascertainable Standard Principal Invasions (HEMS Only). The Independent 
Trustee (or Co-Trustees) may distribute principal from the Marital QTIP Trust to the Surviving 
Spouse ONLY as strictly necessary for the Surviving Spouse's health, education, maintenance, 
and support ("HEMS") in her accustomed standard of living, after taking into account all income 
and liquid resources available to the Surviving Spouse inside the Survivor's Trust (Trust A).
Section 1.04 Prohibition on Beneficiary Modification or Diversion. The Surviving Spouse 
shall have NO inter vivos or testamentary general or limited power of appointment over the 
Marital QTIP Trust, and may not pledge, assign, or divert any principal of the Marital QTIP Trust 
to a subsequent spouse, stepchildren, or third parties.
Section 1.05 Remainder Upon Death of Surviving Spouse. Upon the death of the Surviving 
Spouse, any accrued and undistributed net income shall be distributed to the Surviving 
Spouse's estate, and the entire remaining principal of the Marital QTIP Trust shall be transferred 
to the Staggered Children's Sub-Trusts (Part II) and/or Special Needs Trust for the Deceased 
Grantor's designated descendants.

Part II: STAGGERED DISTRIBUTION CHILDREN'S SUB-TRUSTS (AGES 25 / 
30 / 35)
Section 2.01 Division into Separate Shares. Upon the triggering distribution event, the trust 
estate allocated to the Children's Sub-Trusts shall be divided into separate, equal shares (per 
stirpes) for Harrison Montgomery and Beatrice Vance (excluding Ethan Montgomery, whose 
share is specifically directed to his Third-Party Special Needs Trust). Each child's share shall be 
held and administered as a separate sub-trust.
Section 2.02 Discretionary HEMS Distributions Prior to Full Vesting. Until a child's separate 
sub-trust is fully distributed, the Trustee shall pay to or apply for the benefit of the child so much 
of the net income and principal of the child's sub-trust as the Trustee, in its sole discretion, 
deems necessary or advisable for the child's health, higher education, maintenance, and 
support ("HEMS").
Section 2.03 Early Principal Advancement Milestones. Prior to full termination, the Trustee is 
authorized in its discretion to advance principal to a beneficiary for: (a) The purchase of a 
primary residence (up to 20% of the sub-trust value); or (b) The acquisition or startup of a bona 
fide business or professional practice upon presentation of a formal business plan.
Section 2.04 Mandatory Staggered Age Distributions (1/3 — 1/3 — 1/3). Subject to the 
Holdback Guardrails in Section 2.05, the Trustee shall make outright distributions of principal to 
each child upon attaining the following ages:
Milestone Age Required Fraction of 
Remaining Principal
Practical Equivalent
Age Twenty-Five (25) One-Third (1/3) of the then-
current principal balance
First 1/3 installment
Age Thirty (30) One-Half (1/2) of the then-
remaining principal balance
Second 1/3 installment
Age Thirty-Five (35) All (100%) of the remaining 
balance of the sub-trust
Final 1/3 installment
Section 2.05 Substance Abuse, Gambling & Creditor Holdback Clause. Notwithstanding 
Section 2.04, if the Trustee reasonably believes that a beneficiary is (a) dependent upon or 
abusing alcohol, illegal drugs, or prescription medications, (b) engaged in compulsive gambling, 
(c) a defendant in a pending lawsuit or bankruptcy proceeding, or (d) party to a pending divorce 
action, the Trustee SHALL suspend any mandatory age-based principal distribution until the 
condition is resolved.
APPROVED AND EXECUTED as an integral Sub-Trust Charter on this 12th day of November, 
2026.

RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY, Grantor & Trustee

THIRD-PARTY SUPPLEMENTAL / SPECIAL NEEDS TRUST
For the Sole Benefit of ETHAN MONTGOMERY
THIS THIRD-PARTY SPECIAL NEEDS TRUST AGREEMENT (the "Trust Agreement") is 
established this 12th day of November, 2026, by and between RICHARD STERLING 
MONTGOMERY and ELEANOR VANCE MONTGOMERY (the "Grantors") and JULIAN M. 
MONTGOMERY (the "Trustee"), for the lifelong supplemental benefit of ETHAN 
MONTGOMERY, born November 5, 2015 (the "Beneficiary").
Article I: THIRD-PARTY ORIGIN & NON-PAYBACK DECLARATION
Section 1.01 Third-Party Funding Only. This Trust is a third-party supplemental needs trust 
funded exclusively with assets belonging to the Grantors (via inter vivos gifts, life insurance 
proceeds, or pours/transfers from The Montgomery Revocable Living Trust). NO assets 
belonging to the Beneficiary (such as personal injury settlements, back-pay awards, or direct 
inheritances) shall ever be commingled with or accepted into this Trust.
Section 1.02 No Medicaid Payback Required. Because this is a Third-Party Special Needs 
Trust and not a self-settled trust under 42 U.S.C. § 1396p(d)(4)(A), upon the death of the 
Beneficiary, the State Medicaid agency shall have NO claim for reimbursement against the 
remaining principal, which shall pass directly to the Grantors' remainder beneficiaries named in 
Article IV.
Article II: SUPPLEMENTAL NEEDS PURPOSE & PRESERVE BENEFITS 
MANDATE
Section 2.01 Intent of Grantors — Supplement, Never Supplant. It is the primary intent of 
the Grantors that the assets of this Trust be used to supplement, and NEVER to supplant, 
impair, or diminish, any federal, state, local, or private means-tested government assistance or 
benefits for which the Beneficiary may be eligible or receiving, including but not limited to 
Supplemental Security Income ("SSI"), Medicaid, Waiver Programs, HUD Section 8 housing 
assistance, or state disability services.
Section 2.02 Purely Discretionary Supplemental Distributions. The Trustee may pay to or 
apply for the benefit of the Beneficiary such amounts from the net income or principal of the 
Trust as the Trustee, in its SOLE, ABSOLUTE, and UNFETTERED DISCRETION, deems 
advisable to provide for the Beneficiary's nonsupport supplemental needs. The Beneficiary shall 
have NO legal right to demand, compel, or direct any distribution from this Trust.
Section 2.03 Permitted Quality-of-Life Expenditures. Permissible supplemental distributions 
paid directly to third-party vendors include, by way of illustration:
• Medical, dental, rehabilitative, behavioral, or physical therapy services and assistive 
technology not covered by Medicaid;
• Private case management, companion care, caregiver respite, and advocacy services;
• Wheelchair-accessible vehicles, vehicle maintenance, insurance, and transportation;

• Computers, electronics, internet/phone service, hobby supplies, recreation, vacations, and 
travel expenses;
• Contributions to a qualified ABLE Account (IRC § 529A) owned by the Beneficiary up to the 
annual federal gift tax limit.
Section 2.04 Strict Prohibition on Direct Cash & ISM Guardrails. The Trustee shall NEVER 
distribute unrestricted cash directly to the Beneficiary. Prior to paying for any food or shelter 
item that could be classified by the Social Security Administration as "In-Kind Support and 
Maintenance" ("ISM") under the Presumed Maximum Value (PMV) rules, the Trustee shall 
evaluate whether such payment would reduce or eliminate the Beneficiary's SSI or linked 
Medicaid eligibility.
Article III: SPENDTHRIFT, EMERGENCY TERMINATION & SAVINGS 
CLAUSES
Section 3.01 Spendthrift & Non-Countable Resource Clause. No part of the principal or 
income of this Trust shall be considered an available resource to the Beneficiary for government 
benefit eligibility purposes, nor shall it be subject to the claims of any public agency or private 
creditor.
Section 3.02 Administrative Amendment Power for Statutory Changes. The Independent 
Trustee is authorized to amend the administrative or distribution provisions of this Trust without 
court approval to the extent strictly necessary to comply with changes in Social Security 
(POMS) or Medicaid laws and regulations so as to preserve the Beneficiary's eligibility.
Article IV: TERMINATION UPON DEATH OF BENEFICIARY
Section 4.01 Final Remainder Distribution. Upon the death of the Beneficiary, the Trustee 
may pay the Beneficiary's funeral and burial expenses, and shall distribute all remaining 
principal and undistributed income free of government payback claims to:
• Harrison Montgomery (50%); and
• Beatrice Vance (50%), per stirpes.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Grantors and Trustee have executed this Third-Party Special 
Needs Trust Agreement on the date first written above.
__________________________________________________
RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY, Grantor
__________________________________________________
ELEANOR VANCE MONTGOMERY, Grantor
__________________________________________________
JULIAN M. MONTGOMERY, Trustee

STATE OF TEXAS

TRUST-INTEGRATED INCAPACITY SUITE & CERTIFICATE 
OF TRUST
Durable Financial POA, Advance Directive, HIPAA & Abstract of Trust
PURPOSE OF THIS COMPREHENSIVE INCAPACITY SUITE: In a Medium-Complexity Estate 
Plan centered around a Revocable Living Trust, standard incapacity documents must be 
explicitly coordinated with the Trust. This file contains: (Part I) A Trust-Integrated Durable 
Financial Power of Attorney authorizing your Agent to transfer forgotten assets into your 
Revocable Living Trust if you become incapacitated prior to death; (Part II) A Coordinated 
Medical Power of Attorney, Living Will & HIPAA Release; and (Part III) A Certification / Abstract 
of Trust to present to banks and out-of-state title companies without exposing private blended-
family or Special Needs distribution terms.
Part I: TRUST-INTEGRATED DURABLE FINANCIAL POWER OF ATTORNEY
Section 1.01 Appointment of Financial Agent. I, RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY, 
residing at 1042 River Oaks Blvd, Houston, TX 77019, appoint my spouse, Eleanor Vance 
Montgomery, as my Primary Financial Agent. If my spouse is unable or unwilling to serve, I 
appoint Julian M. Montgomery as First Alternate Financial Agent, and Clara Vance as Second 
Alternate Financial Agent.
Section 1.02 Express Authority to Fund Revocable Living Trust. In addition to all statutory 
general powers over real estate, banking, securities, retirement accounts, taxes, and digital 
assets, my Agent is EXPRESSLY AUTHORIZED to convey, assign, transfer, and retitle any of 
my real or personal property into "THE MONTGOMERY REVOCABLE LIVING TRUST, dated 
November 12, 2026" so as to complete the funding of my Trust and prevent probate during any 
period of my incapacity. However, my Agent shall have NO power to amend, revoke, or alter the 
dispositive sub-trust terms (QTIP, Children's, or Special Needs Sub-Trusts) of said Trust.
Section 1.03 Durability & Effective Date. This Power of Attorney is durable and shall not be 
affected by my subsequent disability or incapacity. [ X ] Effective Immediately.
Part II: COORDINATED HEALTHCARE POA, LIVING WILL & FAMILY HIPAA 
RELEASE
Section 2.01 Healthcare Proxy Appointment. If I am unable to make medical decisions, I 
appoint Eleanor Vance Montgomery (Phone: (713) 555-0192) as my Healthcare Agent, and 
Julian M. Montgomery (Phone: (512) 555-0143) as Alternate Healthcare Agent.
Section 2.02 Blended Family Visitation & HIPAA Access. To prevent family conflict during 
hospitalization, I authorize all physicians and hospitals under HIPAA (45 C.F.R. § 164.508) to 
release medical status updates to my Healthcare Agent AND to the following family members: 
Eleanor Vance Montgomery, Harrison Montgomery, and Clara Vance.

Section 2.03 End-of-Life Living Will Directive. If certified by two physicians to have a terminal 
condition or irreversible coma/persistent vegetative state: [ X ] Withhold artificial life-prolonging 
procedures and provide maximum palliative comfort care.
Part III: CERTIFICATION OF TRUST (ABSTRACT OF TRUST FOR 
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS)
Section 3.01 Statutory Certification. Pursuant to the Texas Trust Code, the undersigned 
Trustee(s) hereby certify the following facts to any financial institution, brokerage custodian, or 
title insurance company:
1. Name of Trust: THE MONTGOMERY REVOCABLE LIVING TRUST, dated November 12, 
2026.
2. Grantors/Settlors: RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY and ELEANOR VANCE 
MONTGOMERY.
3. Currently Acting Trustee(s): RICHARD STERLING MONTGOMERY and ELEANOR VANCE 
MONTGOMERY, residing at 1042 River Oaks Blvd, Houston, TX 77019.
